title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, fully archived, verifier‑grounded paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) comparing a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. Crucially, the preregistered confirmatory generation_semantics for the seed_0 runs supplied a shared canonical candidate to both conditions per pair ("shared_initial_candidate"; see execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), so the primary paired test measures verifier pass/fail on identical supplied candidates rather than independent LLM sampling. Using a deterministic open validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we observed baseline success = 120/120 and gpt‑5‑mini (guarded, seed_0) success = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. These artifact‑grounded results are reported verbatim and explained: the degenerate outcome follows from preregistered shared‑candidate semantics and templated synthetic tasks, not from evidence of LLM robustness under independent generation. We release the full execution, validator traces, and hash manifest (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2..., deterministic_reconciliation.json) and specify concrete, artifact‑anchored next steps for verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation (independent per‑condition sampling, multi‑seed sensitivity, broader task heterogeneity, multiple validator modalities).

sections.introduction: Motivation. Translating operator intent to device configuration with generative models promises productivity gains but raises operational correctness concerns: reachability, ACL/policy preservation, ordering and transient safety. Prior work emphasizes verifier grounding and generate–validate–repair pipelines [10,11,12]. Research question. Under a preregistered, artifact‑archived protocol, does a single‑pass LLM generator yield a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline (paired analysis)? Scope and contributions. We preregistered an executable plan (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, SHA‑256 7db1663c...) and ran the confirmatory experiment with full artifact archiving. We (1) publish the raw model calls and validator traces, (2) report the exact confirmatory outcome (degenerate agreement) and its concrete artifact causes (shared_initial candidates), and (3) give artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑up evaluations that probe independent generative robustness.
sections.related_work: Nearest work. Verifier‑based network analysis and Batfish evolution show the value of high‑fidelity configuration validators for pre‑deployment checks [10]. LLM intent→configuration and intent‑based network configuration research motivates verifier‑grounded evaluation rather than token metrics [11,12]. Our contribution differs by delivering a preregistered, fully hashed execution bundle and by diagnosing a degenerate confirmatory outcome with explicit artifact provenance rather than by proposing new benchmarks or models.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, SHA‑256 7db1663c...) specified N=120 programmatic tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS), two conditions (baseline template, guarded LLM), one canonical seed (seed_0) for the confirmatory paired test, and primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Critically, the preregistered confirmatory generation_semantics used for seed_0 was "shared_initial_candidate", i.e., the same canonical candidate was supplied to both scoring episodes for each pair (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; see execution manifest). Models and infrastructure. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Validator. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) parsed normalized configuration, applied intent and workflow constraints, and emitted binary pass/fail plus detailed validator_trace per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). Execution accounting. Completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial canonical candidate per pair) and no infrastructure failures (execution/execution_manifest.json). Confirmatory statistical analysis. Paired estimator = mean(llm_i − baseline_i) over i=1..120. We computed two‑sided McNemar exact test and 95% bootstrap percentile CI on the paired difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed 1729). All analysis code and outputs are archived (analysis/*). Contamination heuristics. Preregistered string‑overlap rules (exact match or normalized 5‑gram ≥0.95 → suspected_contamination; normalized Levenshtein ≥0.90 → high_overlap) were run and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...).
sections.results: Execution and validator outcomes. All confirmatory pairs completed (complete_pairs = 120). Validator outcomes: baseline_successes = 120/120 (100%); guarded_successes (gpt‑5‑mini seed_0) = 120/120 (100%). Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Paired estimator = 0.00. Bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00]; McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative artifact evidence. The shared_candidate usage is visible in execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...) and in execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...); a reconciliation record (deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms accounting consistency. Statistical note (artifact‑backed). When every paired difference is zero (identical binary outcomes across conditions), the bootstrap distribution of the paired difference collapses to a point mass at 0.00 (hence CI [0.00,0.00]) and McNemar’s test returns p=1.0; these are mechanically correct but uninformative about independent generator behavior and must be interpreted accordingly.
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation. The confirmatory degenerate outcome is an accurate report of what the preregistered pipeline executed, yet it does not evidence independence nor LLM robustness under operational diversity. Three concrete artifact‑documented causes explain this: (1) Confirmatory generation semantics: seed_0 runs used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 examples: 8f38c8be..., ae967f70...), producing identical canonical candidates per pair; (2) Task/validator coupling: the task generator encoded required_sequence and constraints that the validator enforces (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, transformation_manifest.json), favoring canonical solutions; (3) Template regularity: programmatic task synthesis yields narrow solution forms that template‑aligned candidates satisfy. Implications for evaluation. To assess independent LLM generative reliability we recommend, and archive how to run, the following artifact‑anchored changes: (A) switch generation_semantics to independent_per_condition (do not reuse shared_initial candidates) and sample multiple independent seeds per condition; (B) expand task heterogeneity beyond templated sequences; (C) include multiple validator modalities (control‑plane emulation, reachability analyzers) rather than a single deterministic validator; (D) compute seed‑sensitivity statistics (pre‑specified in the original preregistration but exploratory). All necessary code paths and manifest entries to enact these changes are present in the submitted execution bundle and can be re‑run without fabricating new data. On contamination and training‑data exposure. Contamination heuristics were computed and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...), and no confirmatory flags were found under the preregistered metrics; nevertheless, absence of a flag is not a proof of zero exposure, and we state that residual uncertainty explicitly.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered confirmatory protocol (shared_initial seed_0 semantics), both the deterministic template baseline and the recorded gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition produced verifier‑valid configurations on the N=120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). The degenerate agreement is artifact‑grounded and attributable to preregistered generation semantics and templated tasks; it therefore does not generalize to independent LLM generation in operational distributions. We publish the full execution and analysis artifacts (full hash manifest present) so others can reproduce the exact run and execute the recommended independent‑generation follow‑ups. Verifier grounding remains necessary; careful preregistered execution semantics (independent sampling, multi‑seed design, validator diversity) are essential to obtain informative comparisons of generative robustness.

Preregistration: CAND-2026-001-NetConfig-Semantic-v1 (frozen prior to execution); preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37. Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, research‑gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, deterministic validation, statistical analysis, autonomous internal peer review, and manuscript drafting and revision. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Confirmatory generation semantics and provenance: the preregistered confirmatory runs used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" for seed_0; the execution artifacts show the same canonical shared_initial candidate was supplied to both the baseline and guarded scoring episodes for each pair (representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 ae967f70...). This fact is disclosed prominently in Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and is the proximate reason the paired test produced perfect agreement. Contamination detection: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics were computed and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...); no confirmatory flags were found under the preregistered thresholds, but residual uncertainty about training‑data exposure remains (see Limitations). Retry and failure policy: preregistered retry rules allowed up to two automatic retries for infrastructure failures; none were required (execution/execution_manifest.json). Full artifact release: the complete execution and analysis bundle (execution/*, analysis/*, deterministic_reconciliation.json, model_configuration.json, provenance/master_prompt.txt) and a full hash manifest are included in the submission package for reproducibility and audit (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the full artifact manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes).
limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates and transformation rules; this favors regular solution forms and limits generality to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair for seed_0; this reduces independence between conditions and explains the degenerate paired outcome (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 examples: 8f38c8be..., ae967f70...).

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary design used one canonical seed per task (seed_0) for the paired analysis; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses are not part of the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same semantic constraints used to synthesize reference answers, increasing the probability that template‑aligned candidates validate and limiting construct validity for open operational distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: exact proof that the model was not exposed to template artifacts during pretraining cannot be provided; preregistered contamination heuristics (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...) found no flags, but absence of flags is an imperfect proxy.

Single‑model, single‑validator result: findings apply to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded execution conditions and validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); they do not generalize to other LLM families, agentic pipelines, or different validators.
